- When sentiment is consistently low or negative (0.00–0.25), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.00), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is positive (0.67–1.00) and price is trending up, model frequently overfits upward momentum; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 5-day high.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.25–0.67), model shows mean-reversion bias; align forecast toward 30-day moving average if no clear trend.
- Model underestimates prices during early part of 30-day horizon when sentiment is weak; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to first 5 days if sentiment < 0.40.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to forecast higher than true; apply 2–4% downward adjustment to all 30d forecast points.
